result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a page-capped trial with a sandbox, but A gives the correct worst case of $20,000/month, ties it to the tight runway, and says one trial per org or domain to stop repeat signups. A also lists specific things to measure (pages per trial account, trial-to-paid conversion, total trial spend) and says how each should change the cap. B relies on an invented 5% retention rate, never states the full-usage worst case, and only touches on what to measure in its 'would change if' note. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B picks a clear direction and works out the worst-case exposure correctly (2,000 × 500 × $0.02 = $20,000/month). It then proposes a 50-page one-time cap with a budget formula, protections against repeat signups, and specific metrics to track without inventing benchmarks. A also recommends a capped trial, but its sizing depends on an invented 5% retention figure and never states the $20,000 ceiling. A's monitoring advice is thinner, and its only risk is casual users who don't intend to pay; it doesn't mention repeat signups.
